On the hill · Humahuaca, Jujuy

Torre de Santa Bárbara

A surviving chapel tower beside the Heroes of Independence Monument. Plan an exterior visit and distinguish their histories before climbing up from central Humahuaca.

Find the tower on Google MapsBack to the square guide

Heritage of Jujuy

Provincial heritage and context

The Santa Bárbara Tower is a surviving part of Humahuaca’s former chapel. The provincial tourism guide explains that the tower survived the demolition of the chapel and was moved to make room for the sculptural group. Jujuy Law 5360 protects both the tower and the sculpture as provincial historic monuments. The national designation under Decree 769/2019 identifies the neighbouring sculpture, not the tower. Heritage protection does not mean the tower operates as a museum or admits visitors indoors.

A photograph of the tower is not available in this guide.

Planning an exterior visit

1

What to look for from outside

Compare the narrow profile of the former bell tower with the scale of the neighbouring civic monument. Their proximity makes two stages of the hill’s history visible without mistaking the remnant of the chapel for the sculpture’s plinth or figures. The broad staircase leads up the hill to the ensemble; it does not indicate an entrance to the bell tower.

2

Walking from the square

From the central square, first locate the stairs to the Heroes of Independence Monument. If you are comfortable climbing and access is open, take the staircase up the hill and find the tower beside the sculptural group. Pace yourself at altitude, stop clear of the walkway and return along a signed public route. A step-free alternative or vehicle access to the tower has not been verified.

3

Transport and photographs

If arriving by bus or car, plan the hill as an outing from central Humahuaca and ask locally where vehicles may stop. For photographs, use a stable exterior viewpoint and leave room for people on the staircase. Framing the tower and its neighbour together can show two separate landmarks; do not climb walls or enter restricted areas.

Visitor questions

Is the tower the Heroes of Independence Monument?

No. They share Santa Bárbara hill, but the tower comes from the old chapel, whereas the monument is a separate sculptural group.

Can I go inside the tower?

Interior access, opening hours and charges are not confirmed. Plan to see it from outside and follow notices at the site.

Is there a step-free route?

The approach described by Jujuy Tourism has a staircase. No step-free alternative has been verified; ask locally if you need another option.
